\begin{exercise} \end{exercise}

1. ch2:2.58↗ exer:polarization-proof Prove that the polarization identity (2.2) holds for every scalar product. \end{exercise}
Proof

The proof of Lemma 1 used only bilinearity and symmetry of $\langle \cdot , \cdot \rangle $, never positive definiteness: expanding $\langle v \pm w, v \pm w \rangle = \langle v,v \rangle \pm 2\langle v,w \rangle + \langle w,w \rangle $ and subtracting gives $4\langle v,w \rangle $. Since a scalar product is by definition a symmetric bilinear form, the identity holds verbatim.
